newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya Commercial Bank lifts Nairobi bourse index.
newsitem.headline: Kenya Commercial Bank lifts Nairobi bourse index.

text.p: Competitive buying for Kenya Commercial Bank pushed the Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) 20-share index up 10.13 points to stand at 3074.03 on Tuesday.
The KCB share price jumped 10 to close at 79.

"Investors were willing to buy it at even higher price, it's just that as a rule the NSE does not allow share prices to go 15 percent higher or lower than the previous day's closing price," a senior broker said.

Turnover was posted at 26.185 million shillings traded on 715,787 shares from 23.384 million shillings traded on 551,109 shares. Bourse officials said on average prices in the market were picking up, with financials leading in recovery.

Investment Commercial Development Corp traded 304,000 shares at between 35 and 32.25, while National Bank of Kenya traded 25,725 shares at 13.80 from 13.35. Barclays Bank was stable at 97 from 97.50 previously.
"Traditionally, financials have been the most active counter. They are also the highest profit-making sector in the economy," a broker said.

Kenya Airways, whose price has been on a steady decline for the last month, hit an all time low of 7.50 from 8.15. Brokers expected the downward trend to continue as many speculators had flooded the market hoping to offload shares.
"I think it's slowly dawning on people that this is going to be a long term investment -- three years or more," a broker said.

Corporate bonds issued by the East African Development Bank traded at 101.35 percent for the second day in the secondary market. Brokers said the bond market was slow at the moment, but predicted that with interest rates on treasury bills coming down sometime next year, activity should pick up.
